evidence_items.claim: Q1 states a single item with fixed daily sales, random replenishment lead time, fixed order quantity top-up to Q, own plus rented warehouse, lost-sale penalty, and asks for the optimal reorder point.
Q2 provides 36, 43 and 61 ordered delivery-time observations for three products.
Q4 fixes volumes 0.05/0.04/0.10, Q0=6, Q=10 and lead time Uniform(1,3).
The source defines c4 inconsistently across sub-questions (per unit lost sale vs per box-day vs per volume-day).
evidence_items.status: VERIFIED, resolved by explicit dual interpretation rather than silent choice

evidence_items.claim: Q3 requires joint ordering of multiple products with a common random arrival and allocation of limited own capacity.
Q5 is open-ended: random sales plus changing ordering environment.
